Appended.description: Appended records were assigned sequence numbers `[first_seq, next_seq)` at commit timestamp `time`. When `replayed` is true, the response returns the result of an earlier append with the same `idempotency_key`.

BeginRequest.description: Optional operations to execute in the new transaction.

CommitRequest.description: Optional operations to execute before the transaction is committed.

Consumer.description: Consumer cursor state: `seq` is the next sequence number to read, and `lag` is the number of unread records (`next_seq - seq`).

CreateApiKey.description: `rate_limit`: maximum requests per second allowed for this key on each node (defaults to the node per-key limit).

CreateStream.description: Stream names must be 1-128 characters matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`. Records older than `retention_ms` or exceeding `max_bytes` are eligible for automatic trimming.

DbInfo.description: `role` specifies the caller's permissions: `reader` allows reads, `writer` adds writes, and `admin` or `owner` adds database deletion.

DbStats.description: Database statistics at the read version (at most 5 s stale). `levels` lists segments by level from shallowest to deepest; `size_bytes` (including blobs) is counted against `quota_bytes`.

DbSummary.description: `org` is the owning organization, or `null` for personal databases.

DeleteRows.description: Specify either `pk` (deletes a single row and returns `found`) or `where` (deletes matching rows up to `limit` and returns `count`).

Filter.description: Row filter expression composed of `and`, `or`, `not`, or a comparison on column `col`. A missing or null operand evaluates to false for all comparison operators, including `ne`; use `exists` to test for presence. Numeric values are compared by numeric value.

value.description: Omitted for `exists`, an array of at most 1000 elements for `in`, or a non-null scalar.

Headers.description: Map of header names (1-128 bytes) to values (at most 4 KiB), with at most 64 entries.

IndexInfo.description: A `building` index is maintained by writes but cannot be queried until its backfill finishes.

KvChange.description: Key change entry as of the feed snapshot: either a live key-value entry (with `expires_at` if set), a point deletion (`deleted: true`, including expired keys), or a range deletion over `[start, end)` (`deleted_range`, where `end: null` denotes the end of the keyspace).

KvItem.description: Key-value entry. Keys and values that are not valid UTF-8 in `utf8` mode are returned in `key_b64` and `value_b64`. Values stored as blobs larger than the inline JSON limit include only `blob`. An entry with a TTL includes `expires_at` (cluster time in ms) once committed.

NewRecord.description: Specify either `value` (encoded according to `encoding`) or `json` (any JSON value). Maximum record size is 1 MiB.

Op.description: Transaction operation. Keys and values are UTF-8 strings unless `encoding: base64` is set. `ttl_ms` sets the entry or row expiration relative to the commit timestamp; row updates preserve existing expiration unless `ttl_ms` is specified. `update_rows` and `delete_rows` modify all rows matching `where` (up to `limit`) within the transaction write limit and return `count`. For stream operations: `append` assigns sequence numbers at commit (`expect_seq` aborts the transaction with 412 if the stream's next sequence number does not match); `read_stream` conflicts with concurrent appends only when the read reaches the end of the stream, and observes earlier trims in the same transaction but not uncommitted appends; `stream_info` conflicts with concurrent appends; `set_consumer` requires `seq` to be at most the stream's `next_seq`.

OpResult.description: Result of a transaction operation; populated fields depend on the operation type (see `Op`). An `append` operation reports `first_seq` when the transaction is committed.

PasswordChange.description: `current_password` is required for accounts that have a password.

Query.description: Scans the primary key (default) or a secondary index (`index`) using an equality prefix (`eq`), an optional range bound on the next column, a residual `filter`, and pagination via `cursor`.

Row.description: Map of column names to values. `bytes` columns use base64; `blob` columns accept a staged `blob_id` on write and return `BlobMeta` on read.

RowChange.description: Row change entry as of the feed snapshot: either a live row, a deleted primary key (`deleted: true`), or a table truncation (`deleted_range: true`).

Selection.description: Selects rows to modify using the primary key or a secondary index (`index`), an equality prefix (`eq`), a range bound on the next column, and a residual `filter`. `{}` selects all rows.

SessionInfo.description: Authenticated session: `client` is the client address at sign-in, and `current` is true for the calling session.

SetConsumer.description: Must be at most the stream's `next_seq`.

Stream.description: Stream metadata and state. Retained records span `[first_seq, next_seq)` with total payload and header size `bytes` and timestamps from `first_time` to `last_time`. `consumers` includes up to 100 consumers, continued via `consumers_next_cursor`.

StreamConfig.description: Omitted fields keep their current setting; `null` removes a retention limit.

StreamFilter.description: Stream record filter composed of `and`, `or`, `not`, a comparison on a JSON body `field` (dot-separated path where numeric segments index arrays) or `header`, or a `{ "op": "contains", "value": "..." }` substring match on the raw record body. A missing or null operand evaluates to false for all comparison operators, including `ne`; use `exists` to test for presence. Numeric values are compared by numeric value.

value.description: Omitted for `exists`, an array of at most 1000 elements for `in`, or a non-null scalar.
Omitted for `exists`, an array of at most 1000 elements for `in`, or a non-null scalar.

StreamRead.description: Reads records starting from at most one of `from_seq`, `from_time` (first record at or after the timestamp), `tail` (last N records), or `consumer` (consumer cursor, starting at `first_seq` if unset), up to `until_seq` or `until_time` (exclusive). Returns records oldest-first (or newest-first when `reverse` is true), bounded by `limit` (default 100) and `max_bytes` (default 4 MiB, max 16 MiB). When `filter` is set, at most `scan_limit` records (default 10,000) are scanned.

StreamRecord.description: `seq` is the record sequence number; `time` (cluster time in ms) is the commit timestamp of the append. The payload is returned in `json`, `value`, or `value_b64`.

StreamRecords.description: `next_seq` is the cursor for the next page (`from_seq` for forward reads, or `until_seq` for reverse reads). `done` is true when the read reached the end of the requested range. `first_seq` and `tail_seq` are the stream's current `first_seq` and `next_seq`.

TxnResult.description: `appends` lists the starting sequence number assigned to each `append` operation in order.

UpdateRows.description: Specify either `pk` (updates a single row and returns `found`) or `where` (updates matching rows up to `limit` and returns `count`). Existing row expiration is preserved unless `ttl_ms` is set.

info.description: Transactional key-value, table, and stream databases on object storage. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <session token or API key>` (or the `brs_session` cookie). Errors use the Error schema with a stable `code`; `retryable` errors may be retried (use idempotency keys for writes). Requests over a rate limit return 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` and are not applied; writes that would exceed a database's size quota return 507 `quota_exceeded`. Every response includes an `x-request-id` header containing the client-supplied value (1-64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`) or a generated ID recorded in server logs.
